title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: conjugation-doubled mixed-map rho on GT

claims.statement: Fix the challenge point P in G1 and target z in GT. Compute g = e(P,Q0) with one pairing; then z = g^a and the answer is Q = [a]Q0. Run K = 2^20 parallel walks in GT whose step is, by a hash of the current element, either a Granger-Scott cyclotomic squaring (exponent map e -> 2e) or a Frobenius map (e -> p e), with a table addition (e -> e + c_i) on a fraction 1/1024 of the steps. Each visited state emits the pair {y, y^-1}; unitary inversion is a free coefficient conjugation, so one state yields two stored points and two collision event types. Collisions are solved as linear equations in a; the events have distinct solution values because the rare additions make the affine part of the walk exponent vary, which is exactly the property a pure power-map orbit lacks. With T = 2^126.9205 visited states, a stored set of 2T = 2^127.9205 elements, per-state cost 0.43818 target-group-operation equivalents and success probability 0.39, total work is at most 2^125.73 target-group-operation equivalents, including the one-time pairing, chain-start construction, all hashing, table probes, the scalar multiplication [a]Q0 and the final verification. Peak memory is at most 2^138.3 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^20.1 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The attack is classical and cold, uses no auxiliary powers or oracles, and claims no novelty.

experiments.purpose: Check on a toy prime-order group that a collision of two hash-driven walks with exact affine exponent bookkeeping is solved correctly by both linear equations used in proof.md, including the sign-flipped (conjugation) equation. Toy scope only; establishes no production cost, memory or success bound.
